content:
Maya (oncall): Heads up — we're seeing a spike of 502/504s from multiple hosted inference customers hitting /v1/generate. Started ~12:14 UTC, p90 latency jumped and client retries amplified. Can we spin up a quick triage?
Evan - SRE: Acknowledged. Any single-customer blowups or multi-tenant pattern?
Lien - CS: Two paying customers reported: AcmeCorp (acme-prod) and BrightHealth. Both show identical 504s in their traces. They started ~12:15 UTC after a normal traffic ramp.
Rafael - EngRuntime: Pulling runtime metrics now. Early glance shows increased kv-cache miss rate + connection queueing on the primary model pool. Not sure if it's eviction or sudden seq-len distribution change.
support-bot: Ticket INC-3456 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P0.
Priya - EngInfra: Repro from edge:
```
curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"xlarge-rlhf","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":100}' -v
# response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout (after ~30s)
```
Connection traces show requests forwarded to runtime but no reply before gateway timeout.
Rafael - EngRuntime: Recent routing change? I see a small canary that changed model-routing priority 03:00 UTC earlier today. If the canary pushed more traffic into sharded pool it could expose a KV warmup gap. Recommend: 1) rollback canary 2) enable fallback to `xlarge-geo` (lighter) for the affected route.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout detected: route/model-priority-change v0.6 -> v0.7. Initiating canary rollback command per request.
Evan - SRE: While rollback is in progress, enable automatic fallback on gateway for 10% trial to `xlarge-geo` to drain pressure. Command: `infractl route set-fallback /v1/generate xlarge-geo --pct=10`
Maya (oncall): Running fallback command now.
Priya - EngInfra: Fallback enabled, 10% diverted. Observability: queue depth decreased on one shard, p95 latency improving from 2.6s -> 1.1s for diverted traffic.
Lien - CS: AcmeCorp reports fewer errors after ~5m. BrightHealth still sees occasional 504s but lower rate.
Rafael - EngRuntime: Rollback complete — canary reverted. We should keep fallback at 25% until KV warmup completes or we proactively warm caches. Also enabling short-term increased keepalive and slow-warmup feature.
Evan - SRE: Agreed. Actions I want immediate:
- bump fallback to 25% (done)
- temp raise gateway timeout to 60s for in-flight to avoid client-side retry storms (coord with billing)
- run warmup job to pre-populate KV for xlarge-rlhf
Maya (oncall): Implemented fallback 25%. Warmup job kicking off; keeping gateway timeout change on hold — will take approval from infra leads.
Rafael - EngRuntime: Postmortem action items (preliminary):
-Investigate root cause for sudden kv miss spike (likely routing change interaction)
-Add a canary assertion: fail canary if kv-miss-rate increases > 5x baseline
-Add a runtime warmup hook when routing shifts shards/variants
-Improve dashboard: token-level queue depth + ingress->serving correlation
Priya - EngInfra: I'll create tracking tasks in the Infra board and assign:
- TASK-789: Add canary kv-miss guard (assignee: Rafael, due: 3 business days)
- TASK-790: Warmup job orchestration + runbook (assignee: Priya, due: 5 business days)
- TASK-791: Gateway fallback automation + telemetry (assignee: Evan, due: 7 business days)
Evan - SRE: Also propose a short-term mitigation playbook: 1) automatic 20% fallback for rapid kv-miss spikes, 2) immediate canary rollback flag for routing changes. I'll draft OOO snippet.
Maya (oncall): War room concluded — customer-facing comms drafted by Lien, linked in INC-3456. I'll own the postmortem doc and coordinate with Rafael/Priya/Evan for tech writeup. Leaving followups in the ticket and infra board. :thumbsup:
Lien - CS: Confirmed both customers are stable now. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if noise resumes.
Priya - EngInfra: Note: we'll schedule a daytime run of the warmup job to avoid night spikes.
Rafael - EngRuntime: Thanks team. I'll add instrumentation to trace kv-miss causality and share a short RFC for the warmup hook.
Maya (oncall): Closing thread — actions recorded: INC-3456, TASK-789/790/791. Postmortem draft expected EOD tomorrow. Ping me if new regressions appear.
